content.prompt: Solve, by first completing a square.

answer.short:
$x=-2\pm\sqrt3$.

Complete the square and set $u=x+\frac{1}{x}$; only $u=-4$ gives real roots.
answer.worked:
For $x\ne0$,
$$\begin{align*}\left(x+\frac1x\right)^2-2+3\left(x+\frac1x\right)-2&=0\\\left(x+\frac1x\right)^2+3\left(x+\frac1x\right)-4&=0.\end{align*}$$
Let $u=x+\dfrac1x$.
$$\begin{align*}u^2+3u-4&=0\\(u+4)(u-1)&=0\\u&=-4\text{ or }1.\end{align*}$$
For $u=1$, $x^2-x+1=0$ has discriminant $-3$, so no real roots.
For $u=-4$,
$$\begin{align*}x^2+4x+1&=0\\(x+2)^2&=3\\x&=-2\pm\sqrt3.\end{align*}$$
Both roots are nonzero and satisfy $x+\frac{1}{x}=-4$, which makes the original left side zero.

answer.short:
$x=\dfrac{3\pm\sqrt5}{2},\ -2\pm\sqrt3$.

Divide by $x^2$, complete the reciprocal square, then set $u=x+\frac{1}{x}$.
answer.worked:
$x=0$ is not a root. Divide by $x^2$ and complete a square:
$$\begin{align*}x^2+\frac1{x^2}+x+\frac1x-10&=0\\\left(x+\frac1x\right)^2+\left(x+\frac1x\right)-12&=0.\end{align*}$$
Let $u=x+\dfrac1x$.
$$\begin{align*}u^2+u-12&=0\\(u+4)(u-3)&=0\\u&=-4\text{ or }3.\end{align*}$$
For $u=-4$,
$$\begin{align*}x^2+4x+1&=0\\x&=-2\pm\sqrt3.\end{align*}$$
For $u=3$,
$$\begin{align*}x^2-3x+1&=0\\x&=\frac{3\pm\sqrt5}{2}.\end{align*}$$
All four values are nonzero. The identity
$$x^4+x^3-10x^2+x+1=x^2(u+4)(u-3)$$
verifies them in the original polynomial.

answer.short:
$x=0$.

Use $4^x+4^{-x}=(2^x+2^{-x})^2-2$ and solve the resulting quadratic.
answer.worked:
$$\begin{align*}4^x+4^{-x}&=(2^x+2^{-x})^2-2.\end{align*}$$
Let $u=2^x+2^{-x}$.
$$\begin{align*}2(u^2-2)-7u+10&=0\\2u^2-7u+6&=0\\(2u-3)(u-2)&=0\\u&=\frac32\text{ or }2.\end{align*}$$
Let $t=2^x>0$, so $u=t+\frac{1}{t}$. For $u=\frac{3}{2}$,
$$2t^2-3t+2=0.$$
Its discriminant is $9-16=-7$, so this branch has no real solution. For $u=2$,
$$\begin{align*}t^2-2t+1&=0\\(t-1)^2&=0\\t&=1\\2^x&=1\\x&=0.\end{align*}$$
Check: $2(1+1)-7(1+1)+10=0$.
